Order No. 06 Dated: 10.08.2023

Learned counsel for the petitioner, in course of argument, confines his prayer to the extent of issuance of direction upon the concerned respondents to pay appropriate compensation to the petitioner for the structure as well as the land of Survey Plot No. 1219/2,
Village-Ujjaina, Barhi, District-Hazaribagh with respect to Award No. 165 concerning Land Acquisition Case No. 29/2013-14.
2.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that Award No. 165 for Rs.58,15,524/- with respect to the structure as well as the said land was prepared by the respondent no. 5 - the District Land Acquisition Officer, Hazaribagh-cum-Competent Authority, NH-31 under the provisions of the National Highways Act, 1956 in the name of Vinod Keshri and Manoj Keshri (the petitioner).
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that though for the purpose of widening of NH-31, an area of 4.5 decimals out of 5.5 decimals of the petitioner's land was said to be acquired and award was prepared, however, in reality, only 2.5 decimals was acquired, which should be rectified so as to avoid any future difficulty.

Moreover, the compensation to the extent of Manoj Keshri @ Manoj Kumar Saw vs The Union Of India on 10 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51613389/
1 Rs.58,15,524/- was also erroneously calculated ignoring that there was a doble storied fully furnished concrete construction over the said land in which hotel, grocery shop etc. were being run.

sentences.text:
Though there was no other claimant except the petitioner and his brother (Vinod Keshri), still the respondent no. 5 instead of making payment of the awarded amount to them subject to their objection on quantum of compensation, arbitrarily referred the matter to the Civil Judge (Sr.
Division)-I, Hazaribagh under Section 3-H(4) of the Act, 1956.

In fact, pursuant to the petitioner's application dated 13.12.2022 (Annexure-3 to the writ petition) filed before the respondent no. 7 - the Additional Collector, Hazaribagh raising objection against the quantum of compensation, the said respondent should have initiated an arbitration proceeding under Section 3-G(5) of the Act, 1956.

4. The writ petition was earlier taken up on 11.07.2023 and on the said date, following order was passed:
"Mr. Deepak Kr. Dubey, learned A.C to A.A.G-II appearing on behalf of the State-respondents, while producing a copy of letter No. 382 dated 17.09.2023 issued by the District Land Acquisition Officer-cum- Competent Authority, NH-31,
Hazaribagh to the Civil Judge (Sr. Div.-I), Hazaribagh, submits that as per Award No.
165, Rs.58,15,524/- was calculated as compensation to be paid to the awardees i.e.
Vinod Keshri and Manoj Keshri (the petitioner).

However, since there was some dispute, the said case along with 14 other cases of different villages were referred to the said Court under Section 3H(4) of the National Highways Act, 1956 [hereinafter referred to as 'the Act, 1956'].
It is further submitted that the amounts of the respective awards have also been deposited in the account of the said Court through RTGS/NEFT.

As against this, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that there was no dispute with regard to apportionment of the compensation amount, rather the petitioner had claimed more compensation than what was fixed in the award.

Hence, there was no such reason to refer the matter to the Court by the District Land Acquisition Officer,
Hazaribagh invoking Section 3H(4) of the Act, 1956.

Considering the said submission of learned counsel for the petitioner, the District Land Acquisition Officer, Hazaribagh is directed to file specific counter affidavit within two weeks covering the said issue.
Put up this case on 31.07.2023 under the same heading.

A copy of letter No. 382 dated 17.09.2023 is taken on record."
5.

Subsequent to the said order, a counter affidavit has been filed on behalf of the respondent no. 5 on 07.08.2023 stating that the petitioner vide his application dated 13.12.2022 (Annexure-3 to the writ petition), did not get the award of acquired property modified through process of arbitration.
It has further been stated that under the said circumstance, the matter was referred to the competent court and the awarded amount was also deposited in the bank account of the said court.

sentences.text: This Court is of the view that the said stand taken by the respondent no. 5 in the counter affidavit is completely misconceived.
It is nobodies' case that there was any counter claim towards the award prepared in favour of the petitioner and his brother (Vinod Keshri).

On perusal of Annexure-3 to the writ petition, it appears that the petitioner, being aggrieved with the quantum of compensation,
directly filed an application before the respondent no. 7 and, therefore, it was at best a case to be entertained by the respondent no. 7 as an Arbitrator under the provisions of the Act, 1956 on the quantum of compensation, as the petitioner had shown dissatisfaction towards the same.

Nonetheless, the respondent no. 5 had no reason to refer the matter under Section 3-H(4) of the Act,
1956 to the Principal Civil Court of Original Jurisdiction i.e., the court of Civil Judge (Sr. Division)-I,
Hazaribagh and to deposit the said amount in the account of the said court.

sentences.text: 7. Learned counsel for the respondent nos. 3 to 7, on instruction, submits at bar that since the petitioner and his brother were not keen to accept the awarded amount, the same was deposited in the account of the court of Civil Judge (Sr. Division)-I, Hazaribagh along with referring the matter to the said court for adjudication.

8. As against this, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that there is no such document on record to suggest that the petitioner and his brother were not interested in accepting the awarded amount, rather they had raised objection only against the quantum of compensation on the ground that the same was grossly undervalued.

9. Considering the aforesaid aspect of the matter, it emerges that the respondent no. 5 erroneously referred the matter invoking Section 3-H(4) of the Act, 1956 to the court of Civil Judge (Sr.
Division)- I, Hazaribagh in absence of a counter claim by any person except the petitioner and his brother (Vinod Keshri).
10.

Hence, the respondent no. 5 shall issue a letter to the Civil Judge (Sr. Division)-I, Hazaribagh within one week from the date of receipt/production of a copy of this order requesting to de-register the said case (if the same has already been registered) and to send its record back to the said respondent.
11. On receipt of the said letter, the Civil Judge (Sr. Division)-I, Hazaribagh shall send back the record with respect to Award No. 165 in connection with Land Acquisition Case No. 29/2013-14.
An amount of Rs.58,15,524/- deposited in the account of the said court shall also be transmitted back to the account of the respondent no. 5.
The said exercise will be completed within two weeks thereafter.
12. The petitioner is given liberty to file a fresh application before the respondent no. 7 raising objection against the quantum of compensation fixed vide Award No. 165.

On receipt of the said objection, the respondent no. 7, invoking Section 3-G(5) of the Act, 1956, shall proceed further in terms with the said provision and pass an appropriate award within a reasonable period.

13. The petitioner may also file an application before the respondent no. 5 for receiving the awarded amount, subject to the final outcome of the proceeding under Section 3-G(5) of the Act, 1956 before Manoj Keshri @ Manoj Kumar Saw vs The Union Of India on 10 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51613389/
3

On receipt of such application, the respondent no. 5 shall pay the said awarded amount to the petitioner and his brother (Vinod Keshri) on their due identification within two weeks from the date of filing of such application.
14. The writ petition is disposed of with aforesaid direction.
